key_insight: A variational, label-free graph neural network can model heterogeneous solid mechanics by encoding material interfaces in the mesh and minimizing discrete total potential energy, avoiding penalty terms and prescribed interface widths.
engineering_relevance: This makes the method robust for parametric surrogate modeling and inverse identification in multi-material elasticity and hyperelasticity, especially when stiffness contrast is high.
method: Uses a conforming adaptive mesh graph with element-wise constitutive laws.
Trains by minimizing the discrete FE-equivalent potential energy with only first derivatives.
Enforces Dirichlet boundary conditions by construction, with no interface penalty or regularization width.
evidence_signal: Across stiffness contrasts from E_inc/E_mat = 10^-2 to 10^2, the PI-GNN kept von Mises error below 3.58% and achieved 0.49% displacement error versus 7.66% for a strong-form PINN.
watch_item: The approach is computationally more expensive than a single finite-element solve, so its main value is as a surrogate or inverse solver rather than a replacement for one-off analysis.
paper_title: A variational physics-informed graph neural network for heterogeneous solid mechanics
